Zen at the gate of light and shadow
Senses.Explanation: The gate of light and shadow is the records' visible threshold contrasted with the matter inside the house: people mistake its coarse, shallow business for what is within (光影門頭戶底麤淺底事，將作屋裏事). Elsewhere Xueguan Zhiyin says students "recognize only the gate of light and shadow as themselves" (惟認光影門頭當作自己). The phrase also enters verse as a place not to stop: "do not halt your steps at the gate of light and shadow" (光影門頭休駐足). Hongzhi supplies a notable counter-deployment: "a person who settles the matter at the gate of light and shadow will do" (光影門頭了事底漢即得), then immediately asks how one proceeds before guest and host divide and before an image is formed. Zen thus bends ordinary light, shadow, and doorway language into a recurring label for the visible or reflected threshold that records contrast with the inside of the house, oneself, and the not-yet-formed image.

Senses.Explanation: Straw sandals remain literal footwear while serving as the ordinary equipment and expense of traveling on foot through the Chan record. Footwear woven from grass or straw. In Chan records the sandals belong especially to going on foot between teachers: “to wear out straw sandals” and “buy more straw sandals and travel on foot for thirty years” make the ordinary shoe part of the institutional life of itinerant inquiry. The object also enters named encounters: Deshan turns his back on the hall, puts on his sandals, and leaves; Zhaozhou puts a sandal on his head after Nanquan recounts cutting the cat. Huangbo calls “the patriarchs' dark purport” “worn-out straw sandals” and says bare feet would be better. The corpus records these concrete actions and comparisons without supplying a symbolic gloss for the sandals.

Senses.Explanation: Sandal money is the expense of travelling on foot in straw sandals. In the Huangbo–Nanquan exchange, Nanquan sets gruel-water money aside and asks who will repay the sandal money; later records say a reply saves sandal money or warn against wasting it. Chan turns ordinary travel expense into an account of whether a journey or visit was worth its cost. The Record of Master Zhe’an Fan preserves his warning that someone who lightly throws away good time does not even value sandal money.

To miss it: to let what is immediately at issue pass by without meeting it. Sanjiao Zongyin says that even asking what 'this matter' is has already missed it, and answers Magu's reformulated question with the same verdict. Yuanwu Keqin says the miss occurs in the time of raising an eyebrow; Puzhao Xiaoqin says taking up what is right before one can itself become the miss. Dahui Zonggao tells a questioner that he has missed it without knowing and elsewhere says that opening the eyes misses it and closing them misses it too. Zhenjing Kewen says that merely forming an intention while he comes forward has already missed it. Nanfeng Yunbian answers a question about a matter beyond the standard fourfold alternatives with 'you miss it face to face.' Baima Guixi gives a paired limit: hurry and one misses it, go slowly and one cannot catch up. Baichi Xingyuan contrasts counting that remains plainly exact with casually saying 'I understand,' which misses it. The ordinary verb becomes a recurrent public verdict on timing, attention, and response; no single posture, speed, or verbal formula guarantees against it.
Senses.Note: Frozen-corpus concordance: 1,555 exact hits in 237 files and 232 independent works. One act covers missing, overlooking, and letting the occasion pass. Different triggers—asking, intending, opening or closing the eyes, hurrying, slowing, or claiming understanding—are attested circumstances of the same miss, not separate senses.

Senses.Explanation: A turning word is a response demanded or supplied to pivot a case or stuck encounter. In the wild-fox case the old man asks Baizhang Huaihai to provide one in his place, and Baizhang's answer releases him. Wumen Huikai challenges readers to lay one down at the decisive point of a case. Yunmen Wenyan prizes Baling's three turning words as sufficient repayment of his teaching debt. Xuedou Chongxian asks each Chan guest to supply one to the broken-fan challenge. Baiyan Mingzhe asks an interlocutor for a different turning word that would accord with him. Tianyi Yihuai asks the community to provide one on Shakyamuni's behalf against the demon king. In a reported exchange Shun Bujue criticizes Sheng for winning a monastery with only one turning word while still not having dreamed of the teaching. The term therefore names a consequential pivoting response, not any clever sentence.
Senses.Note: Exact frozen-corpus count: 1,769 hits in 294 files and 289 works. Seven witnesses across five independent works meet the packet floor and cover substitution, challenge, three-word set, case response, alternate response, representative defense, and critical use.
